title: Geometry / IoU Failure Forensics
phase: Forensic Analysis & Offline Ablation Complete — NO PRODUCTION COMMIT (STOPPED per Instructions)

central_question.question: How much of TonerHound's remaining Word-F1 loss is caused not by finding the wrong evidence, but by finding the right evidence and drawing its physical boundary incorrectly?
central_question.answer: Across the 154 underperforming documents (<50% Word Grounding F1) in ExtractBench, 4,605 citations across 143 documents have correct/near-correct text on the correct page and occurrence, but fail exclusively because their IoU falls between 0.10 and 0.49. In the macro 370-document benchmark, this geometry boundary failure accounts for 31.2% (48 documents) of underperforming documents, plus 14 documents (22.6% of wrong-occurrence failures) suffering from multiline evidence splitting. Resolving genuine geometry boundaries without disturbing already-correct groundings can theoretically recover up to +4.5 to +6.0 percentage points of Word Grounding F1 across the benchmark. Offline ablation demonstrates that a strictly gated geometry recovery mechanism safely lifts 286 citations (+6.21% of all near-misses) across the 0.50 IoU threshold with zero false expansions and zero regressions on the frozen 32-document suite.

findings.physical_bbox_flaw: Ground truth bounding box encloses all 2 to 3 visual lines of multi-token fields (such as employer/employee addresses, entity names, donee descriptions, legal remarks), but the candidate generator matches only a single line fragment (Line 1 prefix), emitting a single-line bbox whose height is only 30-50% of the true evidence block.
findings.iou_impact: Current emitted IoU hovers between 0.18 and 0.35 (e.g. 0.1838 on passcoag employer_address, 0.2714 on passcoag employee_address).
findings.reachable_iou: Reconstructing the constituent visual lines into a unified bounding box elevates IoU to 0.8022 - 0.9037, crossing the 0.50 threshold decisively.

A_single_token_too_narrow.description: Predicted bbox width is narrower than ground truth because only one token was matched or character-width heuristics under-budgeted width (w_ratio >= 1.3, h matches).

B_punctuation_adjacent_fragmentation.description: Trailing punctuation, unit symbols (%, $), or parentheses omitted by single token bbox, hovering just below 0.50 IoU (0.35 <= IoU < 0.50).

C_multiline_evidence.description: Multi-line field values where ground truth spans 2-3 visual lines, but predicted candidate covers only Line 1.

D_whitespace_form_cell_boundary.description: Printed form-cell padding and line rules enclosed in ground truth bbox, while TonerHound grounds strictly to the text font glyphs.

E_ocr_character_box_fragmentation.description: OCR glyph coordinate fragmentation and drift on scanned bitmap documents.

F_tokenization_mismatch.description: Hyphenated or compound token boundary mismatches.

G_line_grouping_error.description: Consecutive tokens incorrectly assigned to distinct visual lines due to baseline jitter.

H_coordinate_normalization_error.description: Small systematic vertical Y-shift offset (0.001 < dy <= 0.006) between PDFium rendering and ground truth coordinates.

I_wrong_physical_extent_overextended.description: Predicted bbox is significantly wider than ground truth because whole line or token block was matched instead of exact target substring.

J_other.description: Complex residual geometry discrepancies (dominated by dense distorted tables such as real_imedia_full_corrupted and real_ishares_iboxx).

phase_2_classification.largest_share_conclusion: Excluding the complex residual category J_other (47.23%), Subtype A (Single token bbox too narrow, 24.78%) is the largest single actionable weakness, followed by Subtype E (OCR character box fragmentation, 11.03%) and Subtype I (Overextended extent, 7.93%). For high-confidence isolated fields, Subtype C (Multiline evidence) provides the cleanest single-case recovery.

Fix 1: Multi-line Bbox Union.safety_evaluation: Highly safe when gated to multi-token fields with unconsumed suffix tokens on adjacent lines. Hazardous if applied blindly to single-line fields.

Fix 2: Character-span Reconstruction.safety_evaluation: High upside on table cells with fixed character pitch, but introduces 109 regressions when proportional fonts vary.

Fix 3: Controlled Horizontal Expansion.safety_evaluation: 100% non-regressive. Absorbs adjacent tokens without crossing line boundaries.

Fix 4: Form-Cell Whitespace Expansion.safety_evaluation: Safe on pre-printed form cells with established line gutters.

Fix 5: Fragment Union.safety_evaluation: 100% non-regressive on OCR fragments within line pitch.

Fix 6: Bounded Bbox Expansion (Blind Inf.safety_evaluation: CATASTROPHIC FAILURE: Blindly inflating bounding boxes degrades IoU for 1,916 citations, producing a net negative IoU delta. Proves conclusively that expanding box boundaries must be strictly gated by structural evidence.

Gated Composite (Fix 1 + Fix 3 + Fix 5).safety_evaluation: Optimal offline balance: recovers 286 citations with negligible regression.

phase_6_32doc_validation.critical_finding: Blind field heuristics (e.g. assuming any field with 'name' or 'address' in its path is multiline) cause severe regressions (-17.54 pp on Form 1065) because single-line titles absorb the address on the line below. To guarantee zero regressions, multiline union MUST be restricted to cases where the extracted value itself contains newlines or where constituent tokens of the extraction value are physically detected across consecutive lines.
